scenes.title: What is SQL?
scenes.narration: SQL is the standard language we use to talk to relational databases, and this lesson explains what that really means.

scenes.title: The core idea
bullets: SQL stands for Structured Query Language
It is declarative, so you state what you want
The engine decides how to fetch it efficiently
scenes.narration: SQL stands for Structured Query Language, the shared language every relational database understands. It is declarative because you describe the result you want rather than the steps to compute it. That matters because the database's optimizer is left to choose the most efficient way to retrieve your data.

scenes.title: How a query travels
scenes.narration: When you submit a query, the database parses and optimizes it by checking indexes and statistics. It then builds an execution plan and runs it to gather the matching rows. Finally the result set flows back to you without any low-level logic on your part.

scenes.title: A first query
scenes.code:
SELECT name, salary
FROM employees
WHERE department = 'IT'
ORDER BY salary DESC;
scenes.narration: Here SELECT names the columns we want back, and FROM points to the employees table. The WHERE clause keeps only rows in the IT department. Finally ORDER BY sorts those rows from highest salary to lowest for a focused result.

scenes.text: SQL lets you describe the data you want and trust the engine to deliver it, making it the universal language of data work.
scenes.narration: Remember that SQL is about describing what you need, not how to get it, which is exactly why it remains the universal language of data.
